Rae (design): quick sync 1: batch resource form. two decisions we need: (1) validation UX for dense inputs: show inline errors as they appear or a compact summary up top with anchors? (2) required-field treatment: asterisk only, or explicit 'Required' label for clarity/a11y?
Noah (pm): for heavy workflows i vote summary-up-top + anchors to first error. keeps the page scannable. inline is fine for single-item flows.
Omar (eng): perf note: rendering hundreds of inline error nodes spikes reflow. we can lazy-render inline messages on focus to compromise.
Faye (a11y): asterisk alone isn't reliably announced. prefer visible 'Required' text and programmatic connection (aria-describedby or aria-required). if we keep asterisks, include a visually-hidden descriptor for screen readers.
Rae (design): on copy: current error text is terse: 'Name required'. i'd like something slightly more helpful but short: 'Please enter a name.'
Noah (pm): agree. also need a pattern for destructive actions: typed-confirm vs undo toast. typed-confirm for irreversible deletes; undo for accidental/bulk ones if we can restore.
Omar (eng): typed-confirm adds implementation complexity (focus trap + typed input validation). undo toast is simpler, but backup/restore paths required.
Faye (a11y): typed-confirm must announce instructions clearly and focus the input; also provide alternative keyboard-friendly controls. avoid surprise focus behavior for screen reader users.
Rae (design): proposed pattern: default to a compact error summary with count + anchor links after submit. reveal inline error text when a field receives focus or after the user blurs it with an error. Required marker: show asterisk visually, but include 'Required' in a visually-hidden span tied with aria-describedby; we can also add a tooltip for sighted users.
Noah (pm): that covers most use-cases. for destructive ops: typed-confirm for single immutable deletes (customer PII), undo toast for other deletes with retention policy. let's document the cutoff threshold.
Omar (eng): implementation plan: add aria-live='polite' to the summary container, lazy-mount inline nodes, and reuse .sr-only utilities. I'll prototype in the components lib and test perf on 200-row renders.
Faye (a11y): +1. ensure summary isn't auto-focused; let users opt into it. anchors should move focus only when activated. test with NVDA/VoiceOver.
Rae (design): small poll: react :one: for inline-eager, :two: for summary-first (summary then inline-on-focus).
RedwoodBot: Reaction added :eyes:
Omar (eng): :one:
Rae (design): :two:
Faye (a11y): :two:
Noah (pm): :two:
Rae (design): looks like summary-first wins. I'll mock summary-first (with inline-on-focus) and inline-eager variants and run a 6-person usability quick test. will post clickable prototypes and copy options. tagging @Omar for feasibility and @Faye for a11y review.
Omar (eng): i'll aim for a demo by EOD and benchmark rendering perf.
Faye (a11y): i'll review keyboard flows and screen reader text once the prototype is up.
Rae (design): thanks! planning to land copy update ("Please enter a name.") and component changes after tests. :sparkles:
